An ordered list uses `<ol>` and presents its items in a sequence, usually numbered. An unordered list uses `<ul>` and presents its items without a numbered order, usually with bullets.
Write a CSS comment between `/*` and `*/`, for example: `/* This is a comment */`.
CSS can be applied inline using an element’s `style` attribute, internally using a `<style>` element, or externally by linking a separate CSS file.
Write JavaScript inside a `<script>` element, or include an external JavaScript file with a tag such as `<script src="script.js"></script>`.
Use `link text`. The `href` attribute specifies the destination, and the text inside the element is the clickable link.
`<div>` groups content in a block-level container, making it possible to organise or style that content together.
Add a link element inside the document’s `<head>`, for example: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">`.
The `<table>` element creates a table for presenting data in rows and columns.
The CSS box model represents an element as content surrounded by padding, a border, and a margin.

Common CSS selectors include: - Element selector: `p { color: blue; }` selects all `

` elements. - Class selector: `.note { color: green; }` selects elements with `class="note"`. - ID selector: `#title { color: red; }` selects the element with `id="title"`. - Grouping selector: `h1, h2 { font-family: Arial; }` applies styles to both headings.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<body>
  <button id="changeColor">Change background</button>
  <script>
    function changeBackground() {
      document.body.style.backgroundColor = "lightblue";
    }
    document.getElementById("changeColor").addEventListener("click", changeBackground);
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```
When the button is clicked, the event listener calls `changeBackground`, which changes the page body’s background color.

A transition smoothly changes a CSS property between values, commonly when a state changes. For example, `button { transition: background-color 0.3s ease; } button:hover { background-color: blue; }` transitions the background color on hover. An animation uses `@keyframes` to define changes over time, for example: `@keyframes fade { from { opacity: 0; } to { opacity: 1; } } .box { animation: fade 1s ease; }`. The `animation` properties can specify the keyframe name, duration, timing function, and other settings.
